angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 855,711 km at 89.15 pc = 0.13 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 11.2176 +/- 0.0126 mas (same row, RUWE 0.86): 89.15 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.23 +/- 0.03 solar radii from Marcy et al. 2014, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of Kepler-408 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJS..210...20M/abstract): 855,711 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.08 +/- 0.07 solar masses from Marcy et al. 2014, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of Kepler-408 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJS..210...20M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6104 +/- 74 K from Marcy et al. 2014, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-408 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJS..210...20M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Marcy et al. 2014, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-408 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJS..210...20M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/kepler-408.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.292, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
